name: orcaslicer-mcp
description: Work OrcaSlicer with an AI that shows its working: load models, arrange the plate, tune settings, slice, and understand the result.
long_description:
Connects Claude to a real, running OrcaSlicer (the OrcaSlicer MCP build, which adds a token-authenticated local control API). Load models, arrange the plate, tune and sanity-check settings, slice, and understand the result through per-feature breakdowns, setting explanations, and physics checks, live, with every change visible in the GUI. It can also read your printer's status, print history and settings over your network (history and settings need a Klipper printer); those requests are read-only, and it never sends the printer a command. The slicer, your profiles, and your gcode stay on your machine; the AI model comes from your MCP client, and your conversation goes wherever that client sends it.

Requires: (1) OrcaSlicer 2.5 with the OrcaSlicer MCP plugin (from OrcaCloud or the latest release here), or the OrcaSlicer MCP build from https://github.com/MaxEllis/OrcaSlicer/releases with its Remote API enabled in Preferences, and (2) uv (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), which supplies the uvx command this extension uses to run the server.

api_token.title: Remote API token
api_token.description: Leave empty when OrcaSlicer runs on this computer: the connector finds it by itself. Otherwise paste the token from OrcaSlicer's Preferences -> Remote API (build) or the plugin's Config tab.

api_url.title: OrcaSlicer address
api_url.description: Leave empty when OrcaSlicer runs on this computer: the connector finds its address, port included. For the OrcaSlicer MCP build on another computer (LAN access on there): http://<that computer>:13130.

datadir.title: OrcaSlicer settings folder
datadir.description: Leave empty unless OrcaSlicer runs with its own settings folder (started with --datadir, or a portable copy). The plugin's setup shows the folder when this is needed.

print_outcomes_dir.title: Print outcomes folder
print_outcomes_dir.description: Where save_gcode writes its gcode, and where the outcome store of slice records and finished-print results lives; leave blank to use the shared print-outcomes folder if present, otherwise a folder under your home directory.

allow_keys.title: Allow sensitive config keys
allow_keys.description: Advanced, usually left blank. To let the assistant change scripts, custom G-code and printer connection settings, tick Allow script, G-code and connection edits in the OrcaSlicer MCP build's Preferences, Remote API; that box is enough on its own. This field lists keys this connector lets through without checking that box, for older builds or special setups: comma separated, wildcards such as *_gcode work (post_process, *_gcode, print_host, printhost_*, host_type, printer_agent, printer_model, printer_technology, filename_format). OrcaSlicer still applies its own box.

printer_url.title: Printer address
printer_url.description: Leave blank to use the address in OrcaSlicer's active printer profile. Set it when that address doesn't work from this computer, for example to the printer's IP address. A user name and password can be part of the address (http://user:password@192.0.2.10); percent-encode special characters in them, for example @ as %40. A password in the address is stored as an ordinary setting, not in the credential store, so prefer the Printer API key where the printer accepts one.

printer_api_key.title: Printer API key
printer_api_key.description: Only needed when the printer asks for one (OctoPrint, or Moonraker with authorization turned on).

printer_id.title: Printer name
printer_id.description: The name the outcome store gives this printer. Leave blank to use the host name of the Printer address when you set one, otherwise the printer profile's name, otherwise unknown.
